status: PROPOSAL ONLY; no application or Dockerfile implemented yet
detailedDesign: research-and-architecture.json is updated for Kafka ingestion; erd/01-transactions.mmd is the core model. Import jobs are removed.
chosenProjectRecommendation: Transaction Aggregation API, with fraud and statements as optional extensions; assessment requests one chosen project.
confirmedPreferences: Docker Compose for local service management
Simple core flows before additional features
Kafka transaction streams replace transaction imports and import jobs

flows.name: Transactions
steps: Three mock producers publish independent transaction streams
Application consumes, normalizes, categorizes and persists
Choose customer/account and view transactions and summaries
flows.note: Read-only transaction UI with Refresh/optional polling; no CSV upload, Load sample data action, import jobs or source retry controls.

flows.name: Fraud checks
steps: Apply fixed versioned rules and persist results
flows.note: No case-management or rule-editor UI. Mockup illustrates only the high-value debit rule.

flows.name: Statements
steps: Authorized operator uploads PDF for a customer account
flows.note: Customer account selection can be omitted only in the single-account demo. Implement backend ownership checks and private storage.

simplestBaseline.app: One Spring Boot modular application; TanStack/shadcn frontend built and bundled into the application image.
simplestBaseline.database: PostgreSQL; Liquibase root changelog includes module-owned changelogs.
simplestBaseline.moduleEvents: Kafka is required for input. Persist categorized-event publication through Spring Modulith in the same DB transaction, then externalize to Kafka. Optional fraud module consumes the categorized topic with a separate consumer group.
simplestBaseline.storage: Private mounted volume behind a storage interface for the local statement extension.
simplestBaseline.observability: Actuator, structured logs, consumer lag, duplicates, invalid events and categorized-publication backlog; optional monitoring containers later.

submissionDeliverables: compose.yaml with healthchecks, persistent volumes and externalized configuration
README for build/run/test, chosen brief, architecture tradeoffs and limitations
Automated tests for normalization, categorization, exact money, deduplication, source failures, access control and chosen extensions
OpenAPI contract and deterministic mock sources
qualityNotes: Compose manages the reproducible local setup, not a claim of production HA.
No confirmed-fraud claim from a rule match.
Repeated sample loading must not inflate totals.
Never interpret a missing fraud evaluation as NOT_FLAGGED.
Do not add dashboards to demonstrate behavior already clear through APIs and tests.
Mock producers run in the demo Compose profile and never insert directly into PostgreSQL.
Kafka-to-PostgreSQL delivery is at least once with idempotent writes; no cross-system exactly-once claim.
Existing transaction mockup and original prompt are historical: stream status/Refresh replaces Load sample data and source labels change.
